content:
Apple continues to refine profile support on the Apple TV 4K, and a change related to app access permissions in tvOS 27 gives users another reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict which apps users can launch

Profile support is a common feature on every major streaming platform, and among other benefits it ensures that people living in the same household can keep their watch history and recommendations separate.

Apple has had profile support in tvOS for some time, but it has become more useful over the past year with several updates.

Now tvOS 27 brings another improvement. According to Apple's official release notes:

The change is clearly aimed at parents.

Kids' profiles already let you restrict what they see inside the Apple TV app. That's useful, but it doesn't stop your child from opening another app that has no such restrictions.

Now parents can head into Settings and prevent certain apps from launching altogether while a kid profile is active.

It's a good step forward for making profiles feel complete, and it lines up with Apple's recent emphasis on upgrading parental controls in iOS 27.

Speaking of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple's profile system to the iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about the change in detail here.

Do you use profiles on your Apple TV? What features would you like to see added? Let us know in the comments.
